messages:
Anna: Hi team — incoming from AcmeMaps. After we rotated their API service key this morning two mobile clients are getting 403s while web and server-to-server calls are fine. Customer says: \"we rotated via our CI pipeline, no errors reported, then mobile app started failing within ~10m\" :confused:
Miguel: Can you paste the exact 403 body / headers? Any edge/cache in front of mobile clients? :eyes:
Anna: Paste from customer logs: 
```\nHTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\n{\n  \"error\": \"api_key.invalid\",\n  \"detail\": \"key not authorized for route: /v1/generate\"\n}\nX-Edge-Cache: HIT\nX-Forwarded-For: 34.12.123.4\n```
They also attached a server-side error recorded at rotation time: 
```
ERROR: vault: unwrap failed: permission denied: iam:Decrypt on projects/acme/maps-kms-key
```
Maya: ok that unwrap line is telling. Did CI rewrap the secret against a new KMS key or create a new service account? Sometimes the pipeline rotates the key material but forgets to update the VM/edge node's IAM binding.
Liam (customer): Confirmed we created a new KMS key and updated the Vault rewrite step. CI log shows `vault write transit/keys/acme/latest rewrap=true` success. We did not touch node service accounts. Mobile app uses short-lived bearer tokens via our edge auth proxy, web uses server API key flow.
Miguel: Two hypotheses: 1) Vault rewrap succeeded but the compute identity that runs the edge auth proxy doesn't have kms:Decrypt for the new CMK, so edge can't decrypt new secret and falls back (or rejects). 2) Edge CDN cached old auth/permission state and is mixing token sets (HIT header). Need to confirm which.
Anna: Repro steps I asked customer to run (mobile devs):
```
# from mobile device or repro VM
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <mobile_token>\" https://edge.acme.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
# and fetch vault secret using CI creds
gcloud kms keys describe acme-kms-key --location=global
vault read secret/data/acme/api-key -format=json
```
They returned: `vault read` ended up showing the new ciphertext but when our edge tried to unwrap, we see the iam:Decrypt error in our logs.
Maya: If edge can't decrypt, the proxy might reject requests with 403 rather than proxying to the backend. Ask for edge proxy logs around the request id. Also purge the edge cache for that key namespace to avoid mixed HITs.
Miguel: @Anna please run an IAM simulation or check policy binding: ensure `serviceAccount:edge-proxy@acme-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` has `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` on the new key alias. If not, add it and re-deploy or rebind.
Anna: I asked customer and they confirmed the new key's IAM bindings only include the CI service account and a different app SA — edge-proxy SA was missing. They're adding the binding now.
sre-bot: deploybot: role-binding update detected for serviceAccount:edge-proxy@acme-prod. Reconciler started. :white_check_mark:
Liam (customer): After adding binding and purging CDN edge for `/v1/generate` namespace, mobile requests succeed. Mobile team tested 50 requests, all 200s.
Miguel: Good — root cause = KMS rewrap without granting decrypt to edge proxy SA + cache causing mixed failures. Two action items: 1) Update CI rotation playbook to sync KMS IAM bindings (automation: add `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding` step for edge SA), 2) Add a post-rotation rollback/health-check that hits edge from a mobile-like client to validate decrypt+auth.
Maya: I'll open a small doc in devex with the exact commands and a quick checklist for rotations. Include commands to check `vault unwrap` and `gcloud kms get-iam-policy`. Also recommend a short TTL for edge cache invalidation on key rotation windows. :memo:
Anna: I've sent the resolution notes to AcmeMaps and asked to keep the ticket open for 24h. Customer confirmed their mobile traffic is healthy and will monitor. Closing in 24h if no regressions. :thumbsup:
Liam (customer): Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround! :partyparrot:
